THE advice and instruction on the domestic
use of electricity which is given in the
Display Room at 25 Foubert's Place today
differs from that given in the 1920s. Not only is
there a far greater range of electrical equipment,
but many more types of home are represented,
since interest in domestic electricity has spread
over a far wider public.

colourful national costumes, provided an audi-

using electrical appliances both in this country
and in their homelands. They were especially
interested in refrigerators and in the advantages
of electric food mixers particularly the mincing
attachment, for minced meat is a popular item
in some Eastern countries. Students and Teachers

brief_extract:
The Court of
Common Council is the modern counterpart of
the earlier assembly. This ancient Hall has been
the scene of trials of traitors, remonstrances to
kings and parliaments, receptions for royal
personages and presidents, and the ceremonial
conferment of the freedom of the City of London
on statesmen and heroes. The Lord Mayor's
Banquet is held here every year.

location_standardised: Westminster, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Its hammer-beam roof influenced the design of Guildhall's roof.
brief_extract:
Reconstruction was undertaken in 1862 when
the flat roof was replaced by an open one con-
forming to the mediaeval architecture of the
building. It is probable that the hammer-beam
roof with timber arch was influenced by that of
Westminster Hall, but the question as to whether
or not it should have stone arches was not
resolved until the 1953 rebuilding. Extensive
alterations to the interior included the installa-
tion of a minstrel's gallery at the west end and a
dark oak screen for the east end; a repaved floor;
heating by floor ducts; and lighting by 16
gaseliers.

Gog and Magog are two new wooden giants to replace those destroyed in 1940, and Magog's shield incorporates a phoenix to recall resurrection after fire. The ancestors of the present giants were paraded in the mid-summer pageants of the 15th and 16th centuries and were eventually set up in Guildhall in 1708. According to legend they represent the conflict between the ancient inhabitants of Britain and the Trojan invaders which resulted in the founding of New Troy, upon whose site London is said to stand.

brief_extract: MAY 3rd, 1965, will certainly be a red letter day in the history of the E.A.W. All who were present at our Reception in Guildhall on the evening of that day when Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother honoured us with her presence, will treasure the memory of that wonderful occasion. Perhaps the most moving moment came after the royal procession had reached the dais when the national anthem was played and everyone in that vast gathering spontaneously joined in the singing.

brief_extract: The same dishes can be used for both functions, and since they are pleasing to look at, save time in ‘dishing-up’ and washing-up, and are hard wearing and hygienic, the housewife has all her needs met at one time. This oven-to-table ware has its origin in a Sunderland factory in which a traditional local craft has been preserved and developed, but the invention itself is part of the history of the American railroad. It was necessary to solve a problem concerning railroad brakemen’s lanterns, for with a hot wick inside and cold rain or snow outside, lantern globes were apt to crack and extinguish the light.

The Sunderland firm of James A.

brief_context: Jobling's firm obtained sole manufacturing rights for Britain.
article_title: from Factory - to Cooker - to Table
brief_extract: The Sunderland firm of James A. Jobling, who had made glass since 1885, obtained a licence as sole manufacturers of such glass in Britain and to hold marketing rights in many parts of the world, and in 1921 clear Pyrex ovenware was introduced to the housewife, who shares the benefits of this invention with scientists and industrialists who use this glass for many varied purposes. Modern glass production requires an array of impressive machines.

brief_context: The firm is the largest manufacturer in the Commonwealth.
article_title: from Factory - to Cooker - to Table
brief_extract: One of the ‘stars’ of the Jobling works, the automatic turret chain machine, has in the six years since its introduction produced over 25,000,000 pieces of laboratory glassware. The firm is the largest manufacturer of glass in the Commonwealth, producing 25,000 miles of glass tubing annually which is sufficient to go round the world with some to spare. Handblowing is still the only means of producing most of the items of laboratory and industrial glassware, the largest of which may have a capacity of 200 litres and a diameter of 30 inches, and is believed to be the largest flask handblown anywhere in the world.

brief_extract: After use the uranium canisters are crushed to a fine powder, put into a skip, and sent through a chute to a cooling pond. Here, the spent fuel elements are kept under water for several months to allow the high intensity radiation to reduce to a safe level before being sent in thick-walled coffins to the Atomic Station at Windscale for processing. On enquiring if there was any check on fall-out we were told that a daily test is taken of milk, water, grass and fish.

Context for retail spending statistics mentioned in the text.
brief_extract: Most of us will be a mixture of two or more of these types but with a little heart searching we shall probably find that one type predominates in our make-up. Whatever our shopping character, however, it as well to remember that women are responsible for something like 80% of the retail spending in this country. Let us therefore try to get value for our money and also some fun out of the task of shopping.

brief_context: Generic reference to commercial shopping areas in the UK.
brief_extract:
THE WISE CONSUMER by MARY GEORGE, MBE, DIRECTOR EAW

THE psychologists tell us that there are five different kinds of shoppers. There is the economic shopper who is always seeking the best quality at the best price and who only goes to shops which give the best service, who can be a very respected customer if she is reasonable but can be the terror of the High Street if she carries her zeal for the best buy to extremes; the personal shopper who likes to shop where she is known, to chat with the retailer and his assistants and to say, 'I always ask for Miss X because she knows exactly my size'; the ethical shopper who shops where she feels she ought to shop because she likes to support the 'little man', the co-operative movement, or business connections of her husband; the impulsive shopper for whom supermarts and exhibitions and end-of-season sales were created, and, lastly, the reluctant shopper who shops because she must, goes to the nearest shop and never has the time or the inclination to argue or complain. Most of us will be a mixture of two or more of these types but with a little heart searching we shall probably find that one type predominates in our make-up.

article_title: VISIT TO CHARLES EARLY & MARRIOTT (WITNEY) BLANKET MILLS
brief_extract:
Jones, Press Correspondent, Aylesbury

Before the advent of electricity the wool industry depended largely on water power to drive the mills, and the centres of the trade were frequently to be found along the banks of rivers. The works of Charles Early & Marriott came to the bank of the River Windrush at Witney in 1669 and the now famous 'Witney' blankets have been produced there ever since. Nowadays the lifeblood of the many machines is electrical power, mostly taken from the National Grid.

brief_context: Where the scholarship winner will receive her training.
article_title: The EAW in Trinidad and Tobago
brief_extract: Marlene has a strong social conscience and she is anxious to obtain a training which will enable her to be of real service to the community. As in all developing countries, trained people are scarce in Trinidad and the one thing that everyone said to me after we had announced the name of the successful candidate was: ‘please send her back to us after she has completed her training in Britain’. I hastened to give the assurance that that was certainly our intention.

ANALYSING ADVERTISING
An Interesting ‘Pilot’ Exercise in the EAW Campaign undertaken by the London Evening Branch

The London Evening Branch spent a profitable evening making a study of a wide selection of different types of advertisements from women’s magazines to determine the appeal behind each advertisement. The advertisements cover electrical goods and services, household furnishings, food and drink, and clothing.
